title: R3-A2 — the greeting's character alignment is generated with its own audio, and lib/visemeSchedule.ts turns it into cues
summary: MINIVIC-AVATAR-v1.md §2.2 and §3. ElevenLabs synthesis is not reproducible across calls, so an alignment fetched today against the committed public/assets/minivic-greeting.mp3 would describe a DIFFERENT render and drift without bound. The alignment must therefore come from the same call that renders the MP3: extend scripts/generate-cloned-greeting.ts to POST /v1/text-to-speech/{VOICE_ID}/with-timestamps?output_format=mp3_44100_128 and write app/data/generated/greeting-alignment.ts (characters[], characterStartTimesSeconds[], characterEndTimesSeconds[], sourceSha256) in the same pass as greeting-asset.ts. sourceSha256 MUST equal greetingAudioSha256 and the build must FATAL otherwise — the same three-way pin scripts/build/greeting_envelope.mjs already enforces for the envelope. Then write lib/visemeSchedule.ts (pure, no DOM): graphemeRuns() with the ~45 ordered longest-match rules in §3.2 mapping to the EXISTING 22-entry set in lib/visemeMap.ts (indices 0-21, index 0 = sil) — introduce NO new taxonomy; buildSchedule() emitting {version:1, sourceSha256, durationSeconds, cues:[[tStart,tEnd,visemeIndex]]} with cue times NEVER rounded; visemeIndexAt(). Constants SILENCE_MIN_S=0.06 and MIN_CUE_S=0.04 per §3.4. Measured: greeting is 365 code units over 24.984671 s (14.61 chars/s) → ~201 cues, ~3 kB. COST GATE: exactly one ordinary 365-character TTS call on the already-configured premade voice — no IVC, no cloning, no new voice.

title: R3-A4 — elevenLabsTts content-negotiates /with-timestamps, and a cached bundle still gets its MP3
summary: MINIVIC-AVATAR-v1.md §2 and §2.1. The WebSocket path is REFUSED and the reason is structural, not preference: browser-side wss:// would ship ELEVENLABS_API_KEY to the client (§14 C-7, caught by TC-NFR-SEC and scripts/validate/built_output_secret_scan.mjs) and a Cloud Functions v2 onRequest has no socket to upgrade and hand back — a relay means new persistent infrastructure. The WS is also WORSE on this task's own axis: word-level alignment vs the REST endpoint's character-level. And the latency argument is small: functions/index.js:129 already does Buffer.from(await upstream.arrayBuffer()), so today's warm 0.46 s TTFB is already a whole-utterance figure and no streaming is being given up. Change the upstream URL to /v1/text-to-speech/{VOICE_ID}/with-timestamps?output_format=mp3_44100_128 and re-shape the response ONCE so the client never learns ElevenLabs' schema: {audioBase64, alignment:{characters, characterStartTimesSeconds, characterEndTimesSeconds}}. CONTENT-NEGOTIATE: Accept: application/json -> that JSON; anything else -> today's binary audio/mpeg body with Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 unchanged. Back-compat is a hard requirement, not a nicety — without it the window between the function deploy and the static export is a broken voice for every returning visitor. Never synthesise an alignment on an upstream failure; 502 with no alignment key. Never log key material.

title: R3-A5 — chat answers drive the mouth from their own alignment, and TTS starts on the first sentence
summary: MINIVIC-AVATAR-v1.md §4.3 and §2.3. Replies get NO atlas — there is no photographic footage of Vikram saying an arbitrary answer and inventing one is the fabrication §14 C-7 forbids. They drive the EXISTING vector drawVisemeMouth + VisemeStage GLSL path, unchanged pixels, new driver. Build the schedule client-side from the alignment the function now returns and install it before playAudio. The one lever with measured leverage on the first-word budget is sentence-chunking: issue the TTS call on the first complete sentence of the streamed answer rather than on the whole answer, so the call starts at 'brain first sentence' instead of 'brain done' (measured brain totals 1.157-1.846 s, first token 0.691-0.823 s at the Cloud Run origin, MINIVIC-BRAIN-0-4 §1.3). REJECTED as budget levers: shortening answers (the gaming MINIVIC-BRAIN §2(c) already refused — do NOT lower CHAT_MAX_TOKENS), a lower-bitrate first chunk (ElevenLabs TTFB is generation-bound, not transfer-bound), and any change that moves first byte without moving first word. B2 stays an ESTIMATE of 1.55-1.98 s warm and must be reported as a range, never claimed as a pass. When no alignment comes back, fall back to the analyser AND fire logMiniVicIssue — named, never silent.

title: R3-A6 — the greeting's mouth becomes photographic: a 22-cell atlas cropped from the 4K master
summary: MINIVIC-AVATAR-v1.md §4.2, and read §1.1 FIRST. MEASURED THIS SESSION: the master is 3840x2160, 24 fps, 295 frames, 12.291667 s video / 12.325011 s audio; the greeting MP3 is 24.984671 s. The master is therefore NOT a recording of anyone speaking this greeting and there is NO timeline to align to — the R3 research doc's §2(b)(3) 'align the master's frame timestamps to the greeting' step is invalid and must not be attempted. Build the atlas by VISEME-CLASS REPRESENTATIVE SELECTION instead: (1) contact sheet, ffmpeg -vf scale=384:-1,drawtext=text='%{n}',tile=20x15 -frames:v 1 (295 frames fit one tile); (2) commit data/minivic-viseme-frames.json = {master, masterSha256, crop:{x,y,w,h}, frames:{visemeIndex -> frameNumber}} chosen once by eye, verifying the crop box with ffmpeg -vf select='eq(n\,120)',crop=W:H:X:Y; (3) scripts/build/minivic_viseme_atlas.mjs runs in build and build:static beside greeting_envelope.mjs, emits a 22x1 tile at 192x128 per cell (4224x128) as public/assets/minivic-visemes.webp. Cell order is visemeIndex ascending so sx = i*192 and no index table ships. BUDGET: 540,672 px vs my_avatar.webp's 51,028 B at ~1,222,480 px => ~22 kB ESTIMATE; hard cap is the audit's TC-NFR-PERF 500 kB, soft target 120 kB asserted directly. The master is UNTRACKED (git ls-files errors; .gitignore:196 artifacts/*), so mirror greeting_envelope.mjs's keep-committed-artefact path exactly: if the committed webp exists and masterSha256 is unchanged, keep it and exit 0; FATAL only when nothing safe remains. Draw with two drawImage calls crossfaded by the SAME visemeLerpRef the vector path and the GLSL stage use, so all three surfaces stay in step by construction. A viseme class with no good frame maps to its nearest neighbour and that substitution is RECORDED IN THE JSON — an unfilled cell must never be a black frame.
